audit.why: Lane difficulty is framed as a concede-then-scale lane: Teemo owns levels 1-5, level 6 is the flip, and the sides in the level chart (Teemo x4, Skill at 6, Teemo x2) already match Teemo's own audited page exactly, with ratings inverse (6/7/7/7/5/6/6 against Teemo's 4/3/3/3/5/4/4). No side or rating change — the mirror is already consistent and changing either half would just be reverted.

Spikes are called correctly: level 6 (Riftwalk), Rod of Ages, and two items. Riftwalk's ranks land at 6/11/16 and its cooldown steps 5/3.5/2s, so the level-11 detonation the breakdown names is the rank-2 (3.5s) step, not an item spike — the existing 'Level 6, Rod of Ages, and level 11 are the three detonations' line is accurate as written.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late tells you to 'Q-silence the counterplay'. Null Sphere has never silenced in this kit version.
audit.why: Riot's current text for Null Sphere is 'fires an orb of void energy at a target, dealing damage and interrupting channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' There is no silence, and silence is a flag the kit builder tracks, so its absence is informative rather than unknown. This matters late: a player told he silences will Q a fed carry expecting a lockout and get killed by the ability he thought he cancelled. What Null Sphere actually does is interrupt a channel — which is a narrower, real button.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence. Its other half is a shield that absorbs magic damage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q description; kitFlags has no silence)
audits/top/teemo__kassadin.json (same error found from the other side)

audit.whatIsWrong: Blinding Dart is named repeatedly as 'the clock this lane runs on' but its cooldown is never given, and the text never says the blind stops basic attacks ONLY.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank (Riot lists cooldown '7', not a per-rank string), range 680. Kassadin's Null Sphere is 650 range, so Teemo out-ranges the only spell you can trade with pre-6 by 30 units. Because the blind hits basic attacks, it turns off exactly one thing in your kit — Nether Blade, which is an auto-attack empower — while Null Sphere, Force Pulse and Riftwalk all land through it. A flat 7s is the single most actionable number in this matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart: flat 7s at every rank, 680 range. It blanks the Nether Blade auto and nothing else — Q, E and R all resolve through a blind.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (W description: next basic attack; Q range 650)

audit.whatIsWrong: The text says Teemo 'kites back on passive move speed' with no counterplay attached, as if the speed were unconditional.
audit.why: Riot's Move Quick text: 'Teemo scampers around, passively increasing his Move Speed until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret.' Any damage you land removes the passive bonus. That reframes the kite war: Null Sphere is not only farm, it is the button that takes his disengage speed away before you commit Riftwalk. The one caveat — and it must be stated, not glossed — is that the ACTIVE sprint 'isn't stopped by being struck', so if he presses W the strip does nothing.
audit.corrected: Landing anything on Teemo strips Move Quick's passive speed. It does not strip the active sprint, so make him spend W before you blink.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'Chain your own ability casts to refresh Force Pulse's cooldown'.
audit.why: Force Pulse is not a cooldown you refresh — Riot's text is 'Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up, Kassadin can use Force Pulse.' It is a charge gate fed by spells cast NEAR him, from either side. That means Teemo's own Blinding Dart, cast at you from close range, charges your E for free. Framing it as your own cooldown reduction hides the free charges the enemy hands you, and it is the reason the level-3 'E only charges when spells fly' line in phases[2] is true.
audit.corrected: Force Pulse charges off spells cast in your vicinity, not just your own — his Blinding Dart arms it for you.

audit.why: The blind-does-not-stop-Null-Sphere point in 'early' is right and well stated, and 'a dashless 500-range Teemo' is right on both counts — Teemo has no dash in his kit and Riftwalk is 500 range. Left alone.
51.28% over 39 games. No change; the page does not quote a different figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Nether Blade's quintupled mana refund' — a specific 5x multiplier stated twice.
audit.why: Riot's W text is only 'restores Mana'. No multiplier and no champion-hit bonus is published in the kit file, and the file's needsResearch block is empty on purpose, so an unstated number is unknown rather than confirmed. I removed the invented multiplier without replacing it with a different number.
audit.corrected: Nether Blade restores mana on the empowered attack. No published multiplier.

edits.before: Teemo's window: his blind (Q) negates your Nether Blade autos so you can't proc the W mana refund, and his E poison ticks you while you only have Null Sphere to farm with — concede these levels.
edits.after: Teemo's window: Blinding Dart (flat 7s) blanks the Nether Blade auto so you can't proc the W mana refund, and Toxic Shot ticks on you while Null Sphere is all you farm with — concede these levels.

edits.before: His blind plus passive move speed kite you the instant you step up, and with no W mana sustain you can't trade back, so farm and weather it.
edits.after: Blinding Dart plus Move Quick kite you the instant you step up — any hit you land strips that passive speed, but you cannot reach him yet, so weather it.

edits.before: You can sit under tower with Nether Blade's quintupled refund and the Null Sphere shield eating poison ticks; he pokes but can't kill, so it's a wash.
edits.after: You can sit under tower on Nether Blade's mana refund with the Null Sphere shield eating poison ticks; he pokes but cannot kill, so it stays a wash.

edits.before: Blind your Nether Blade autos so you can't proc the W mana refund, then kite back on passive move speed
edits.after: Blind the Nether Blade auto to deny your W mana refund, then kite on Move Quick speed you never got to strip

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — a maxed Null Sphere and Nether Blade's quintupled mana refund on champion hits let you farm under tower without going dry, but this is not yet a fight. Level 6 is your real moment: Riftwalk blinks you onto him for a Null Sphere + Force Pulse burst, or straight out of a shroom-zoned wave when he tries to collapse. Chain your own ability casts to refresh Force Pulse's cooldown, and bait the blind first — it can't stop Null Sphere, but you want his Q down so it can't peel your follow-up autos. An escapeless Teemo has nothing to answer the blink.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — a maxed Null Sphere and Nether Blade's mana refund on champion hits let you farm under tower without going dry, but this is not yet a fight. Level 6 is your real moment: Riftwalk blinks you onto him for a Null Sphere + Force Pulse burst, or straight out of a shroom-zoned wave when he tries to collapse. Force Pulse charges off any spell cast near you, so his own Blinding Dart arms it — then count its flat 7 seconds and step in on the downtime, because the blind never stops Null Sphere but it does peel your follow-up autos.

edits.before: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Q-silence the counterplay, and leave before the fight even registers you.
edits.after: Stacked Riftwalk Kassadin is the endgame boss: blink onto carries, Null Sphere to interrupt a channel, and leave before the fight registers you.

edits.before: Track Teemo’s Blinding Dart: Blinds your autos — trade with spells while it is up. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s and blinds basic attacks only — Q, E and R still land. Any hit strips Move Quick's speed.

edits.before: Blinds your autos — trade with spells while it is up. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Blinds basic attacks only, flat 7s — trade with spells while it is up, commit the instant it drops.

edits.before: W restores mana and adds a real auto — but you're still farming, not fighting. Give nothing away.
edits.after: Nether Blade adds mana and a real auto — but Blinding Dart blanks it on a flat 7s. Farm, don't fight.

notes: The invented Null Sphere silence has leaked onto Kassadin's OWN page (breakdown.late, 'Q-silence the counterplay') — worth grepping every champ-data file for 'silence' near 'Null Sphere'. Two other repo-wide patterns showed up here and recur across the whole Kassadin slice: 'Void Stone's 15% magic reduction' (Riot publishes no figure — I left the number in place rather than replace one unverifiable claim with another, but it should be sourced or dropped everywhere at once) and 'Nether Blade's quintupled mana refund' (no multiplier in Riot's text; removed where I touched the string). Also: Teemo's Noxious Trap carries a 'knockup' derived flag in the kit file that contradicts Riot's own description (slow + damage over time only) — treat it as a tooltip-parsing misfire, not a real displacement.
